"To x, y is unto z" is valid- it's equivalent to "to x, y is almost z". Metaphor vs simile and all that stuff.

Really if you want to get technical "are like unto" is a little redundant even in archaic English, it just pops up a lot because it was used in some of the more flowery translations of the Bible.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
New comment, having had the chance to fully read the hub intro text.

I think it's fantastic. Very, very different from what I read before — much briefer, cooler, and less limiting, while keeping all the parts that were good in the draft.

Small note on the Hand — because the Hand is, of course, a thing I've spent too much time thinking of—

I think it could be fun to point out that within the no-violence confines of the Library, pragmatic or desperate Hand members do represent a small but valuable market for certain items that MC&D (or, "The Merchants") can provide, despite the open hostility outside the "safety" of the Library's boundaries.

Related note: in fact, in WL "canon" (which the new Serpent's Hand stuff can probably be considered in the same universe as, along with Black Queen etc), the person or people or thing or things called Dark has probably done the Library itself quite a few favors (see the "Of the Merchants" entry here), and therefore is probably in pretty good standing with the Librarians. (So long as MC&D continues to resist stealing any books, presumably.)

Format critique:

I think it looks very convincing, and I think it's generally speaking pretty good. But it's a bit difficult to read, and it seems like it would be pretty hard to write for.

I think the biggest problem for me from a writing standpoint is that you have to come up with a lot of numbers that most people won't even read. And I mean a lot.

However, it passes the "would I be willing to write for this" test (yes, I would), so it's not a bad format IMO. Just feel it could be tweaked a little. Make some of that info optional if the author wants to focus more on the content. You do emphasize that the item entries need to tell a story, but… the format could be a little more suited to making that happen.

EDIT (again): For me, a generic suggested price list for types of items would help a lot.

Also, small easy-to-fix issue: The paragraph starting with "To MC&D, the most important part of an object is who has it: keeping track of every object as it changes hands." is wall of texty enough that I skipped it twice on instinct. I actually think the first sentence should be its own paragraph (or the first two sentences).
